text: Past performance is not indicative of future results. All investments involve risk, including the possible loss of principal.
This material is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment, legal, or tax advice. Please consult your own advisors before making any financial decisions.
Advisory services are offered through [Firm Name], a registered investment adviser. Fees and expenses will reduce returns.
This communication is intended solely for the individual(s) named above and may contain confidential information. If you received this in error, please notify the sender immediately.
Diversification does not guarantee a profit or protect against loss in a declining market.
Any tax information contained herein is not intended to be used, and cannot be used, for the purpose of avoiding penalties under applicable tax law. Consult a qualified tax professional.
Insurance products are not deposits, are not FDIC insured, are not guaranteed by any bank, and may lose value.
This proposal is not a binding offer and is subject to change without notice. Final terms will be set out in the executed agreement.
Hypothetical or model performance results have inherent limitations and do not reflect actual trading. Results may not reflect the impact of material economic and market factors.
The information provided does not constitute a solicitation to buy or sell any security in any jurisdiction where such solicitation would be unlawful.
Social media posts by advisors must include a disclosure that the content is for educational purposes only and is not personalized investment advice.
Client meeting notes documenting investment recommendations must reference the client's stated risk tolerance and investment objectives on file.
We maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect client information, but we cannot guarantee that our systems will never be compromised by unauthorized access.
Our privacy policy describes how we collect, use, and share personal information, and explains the choices available to clients regarding that information.
Recommendations generated through automated or algorithm-based tools rely on the information provided by the client and may not account for circumstances outside that data set.

Applying environmental, social, and governance criteria to an investment strategy may result in excluding certain sectors or securities, which can affect diversification and performance relative to a broader benchmark.
Digital assets and cryptocurrencies are highly volatile, are largely unregulated, and an investor could lose the entire amount invested.
Options trading involves substantial risk and is not suitable for all investors. Certain options strategies may expose an investor to potentially unlimited losses.

Trading on margin involves risk, including the possibility of losing more than the amount originally invested, and the firm may liquidate positions without prior notice if margin requirements are not met.
Investing in foreign securities involves additional risks, including currency fluctuations, political and economic instability, and less regulatory oversight than in domestic markets.
Alternative investments may be illiquid, may have a limited secondary market, and an investor may not be able to sell or redeem their investment when desired.
Tax-loss harvesting strategies do not guarantee a specific tax outcome and are subject to wash sale and other tax rules that may limit the intended benefit.
Before rolling over a retirement account, clients should compare the fees, services, and investment options of the existing plan against those of the receiving account.
Withdrawing funds from an annuity before the end of the surrender period may result in a surrender charge and the loss of a portion of the amount originally invested.
Outstanding loans against a life insurance policy will reduce both the available cash value and the death benefit payable to beneficiaries.
Structured products may involve derivatives, have complex payout structures, and are subject to the credit risk of the issuing institution.

The firm maintains a business continuity plan intended to permit the resumption of operations after a significant disruption, but cannot guarantee uninterrupted access to accounts or services in every circumstance.
Clients who wish to file a complaint may contact the appropriate regulatory authority; certain account agreements may require disputes to be resolved through arbitration rather than in court.
When an advisor recommends a proprietary product offered by the firm, the firm may receive additional compensation as a result, which presents a conflict of interest.
The firm may pay or receive a referral fee in connection with introducing a client to another professional or service, which presents a potential conflict of interest.
The firm seeks best execution when placing client trades but cannot guarantee that the best possible price will be obtained on every transaction.
Short selling involves the risk of theoretically unlimited loss, is subject to margin requirements, and a lender may recall the borrowed security at any time.
Investments in private funds may be subject to lock-up periods during which withdrawals or redemptions are restricted or unavailable.
A portfolio's actual allocation may drift from its target weights between scheduled rebalancing dates due to market movement.
Research or commentary provided by third-party sources has not been independently verified by the firm and does not necessarily reflect the firm's own views.
In the event of a security incident affecting client information, the firm will provide notification in accordance with applicable law.
